info.title: GridOps Fleet, Operations and Runner Pool API
info.description:
Machine-readable contract for `/api/v1/fleet`, `/api/v1/operations`, and the runner-pool routes that accept an API token.

Browser routes authenticate with the dashboard session cookie or, where marked, a scoped API token (`Authorization: Bearer gat_...`). A request carrying both a cookie and a bearer token is refused. Every route that needs a signed-in user but is not marked with a token scope, here or elsewhere in GridOps, refuses any bearer token with `403 token_not_accepted` before doing anything, instead of answering as a signed-out caller. Agent routes are the host-agent protocol and use a host credential, never an API token.

See docs/fleet-api.md for the human contract, including the authoritative "Who may call what" table of every route, and docs/fleet-automation.md for bot-driven automation.

bearerAuth.description: Scoped API token: `gat_` followed by 43 base64url characters. Created by an administrator; scopes are fleet:read, fleet:enroll, fleet:approve, fleet:operate, fleet:retire, pools:read and pools:manage. No scope implies another. The owner must still be a system administrator on every request.

cookieAuth.name: gridops_session
cookieAuth.description: Dashboard session cookie from GitHub OAuth sign-in.

hostCredential.description: A 43-character host credential issued at enrollment. Never valid on browser routes.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Replaying a key with the same body returns the original result; a different body is an idempotency_conflict.

HostDeleteBlocker.description: Why a machine cannot be deleted yet. A refusal lists every reason that applies.

HostRetireBlocker.description: Why an API token may not retire a machine yet. A refusal lists every reason that applies, in this order.

StartGate.description: Why a machine takes no new runners: it failed `failures` runner starts in the last `windowMinutes` minutes with no successful start since. It is reconsidered at `until`, or sooner if a start on it succeeds. Only new placements skip it; its lifecycle and running jobs are unchanged.

message.description: For example "Not accepting new runners: 3 start failures in the last 15 minutes."

PlacementFailureGroup.description: Placements on one host that failed for the same reason in the last 24 hours.

reason.description: Why the placement failed. Derived from facts the server had when it failed; `unknown` when no cause was available or the code is not recognised.

code.description: The one-time enrollment code; shown exactly once.

consumedHostId.description: Correlates the code with its host; poll until set.

cpuMillis.description: CPU in thousandths of a core, at most what the machine reports.

memoryMib.description: Memory in MiB, at most what the machine reports.

diskBytes.description: Disk in bytes, at most what the machine reports.

allowDockerSocket.description: Hands jobs root-equivalent host access through the Docker socket; deliberate opt-in.

TartHost.description: The Tart host's macOS VM slots, as the runner manager arbitrates them (`docs/design/mac-vm-slots.md`). Pools, and runners of pools, the caller may not see are reported with `poolHidden: true` and no id or name. Signed out, `authenticated` is `false` and everything else is `null` or `unknown`.

authenticated.description: Present, and `false`, only for a caller that is not signed in.

tartAgent.description: `available`: the manager read the Tart agent's health. `unavailable`: a Tart agent is configured but the manager cannot reach it. `not_configured`: the manager has no Tart agent. `unknown`: the runner manager itself could not be asked (or the caller is signed out).

message.description: For `unavailable`, the runner manager's reason. For `unknown` (signed in), always `The runner manager could not be reached.`: the request error, which can name the manager's internal address, is only logged. Otherwise `null`.

slotSetting.description: The GridOps setting "macOS VM slots on the Tart host" (`macosVmSlots`). The manager's `slots.limit` follows it once the reconciler has sent the policy.

slots.description: Present when `tartAgent` is `available` and the agent reports its slots.

limit.description: The slot limit the runner manager enforces.

inUse.description: GridOps VMs running, other software's VMs, and starts in flight.

detection.description: How the agent found other software's VMs; `null` from an agent that predates it.

agentMaxRunners.description: The Tart agent's own cap on GridOps runners (`GRIDOPS_TART_MAX_RUNNERS`).

warning.description: Set when `agentMaxRunners` is below `limit`: the lower of the two wins.

holders.description: Who holds each slot in use: GridOps runners whose VMs run (oldest first), VMs other software runs, then starts in flight. A runner the manager counts but does not name (an agent that predates naming them) is listed with every name `null`.

queue.description: Pools waiting for a slot, head of the line first.

waitingSince.description: When the pool joined the line, by the runner manager's clock.

oneOf.description: A GridOps runner: `runner` once its VM runs, `starting` while it is being started.

since.description: When GridOps began starting the runner.

ApiErrorBody.description: The error body of the session and webhook routes (`gridops-api`'s `ApiError`), not the fleet `ErrorResponse`.

code.description: A stable machine-readable code, when the error has one.

ApiInvalidBody.description: A 422 of the session routes (`gridops-api`'s `ApiError::Invalid`): the `ApiErrorBody` fields plus `details`, which say where the request is wrong.

details.description: Where the request is wrong; for the job category rules, `[{position, message}]`, one per rule whose pattern does not compile.

JobCategory.description: A stored job category. `fix-agent` is counted from fix placements and is never a rule's category.

JobCategoryField.description: The field a rule's pattern is matched against; `labels` matches when any one label matches.

rules.description: The whole list, in order; the first rule that matches a job decides its category. At most 200 rules.

pattern.description: A case-insensitive regular expression, at most 1 KiB (1,024 bytes of UTF-8; `maxLength` counts characters, so a pattern of multi-byte characters is refused sooner).

GitlabConnection.description: A GitLab connection: one project or group on one GitLab instance. It never carries the access token, the webhook secret or the webhook URL.

baseUrl.description: The GitLab instance, normalised: scheme, host, optional port and path, no trailing slash.

scopeId.description: The GitLab project or group id.

canManage.description: Whether the caller may create connections.

scopePath.description: The project or group path, resolved to its id at GitLab.

accessToken.description: A GitLab access token (`glpat-...`); stored encrypted and never returned.

GitlabConnectionCreated.description: The only response that carries the webhook secret, apart from a rotation.

webhookSecret.description: Shown once; configure it as the GitLab webhook's secret token.

UpdateGitlabConnectionRequest.description: A partial update: fields left out are unchanged.

GitlabWebhookSecret.description: A newly issued webhook secret. The previous secret stops working.

value.message: The host changed since it was read.
Machine cannot be retired with an API token yet
This route does not accept API tokens

ErrorResponse.description: Fleet error envelope; see the code table in docs/fleet-api.md.

200.description: Host detail (projection `host`). The `host` projection also carries `failedPlacementsLastHour` (integer), `recentPlacementFailures`, the last 24 hours of recorded placement failures grouped by reason, newest group first (see `PlacementFailureGroup`), and `startGate`, set while the machine takes no new runners because it keeps failing to start them and `null` otherwise (see `StartGate`).

duplicateHardwareOf.description: Other approved, unretired machines reporting the same hardware that the reader may see, so the stale record is easy to tell from the live one.

delete.description: Permanently removes a machine that can never take work again from the machine list, the counts and capacity. Allowed for a retired machine, or one that never finished enrolling (not approved) and has not reported in for 90 seconds. Refused with `409 host_not_deletable` while the machine is approved but not retired, still reporting in, holds an unrevoked credential (approved machines), or still has a placement that is not cleaned up, an unconfirmed start, capacity still charged, a runner that has not finished, or a command waiting within its deadline; `details.reasons` names every reason that applies. The delete is soft: placements, events, samples and audit history stay, and the machine's credential, open recovery codes and grants are revoked. An agent still using the machine's credential is rejected as `unauthenticated` and cannot recreate it. Enrolling the computer again creates a new record. The audit row `fleet.host.deleted` names the actor (and the API token name when one was used), the machine's name and id, and its last heartbeat. Deleting a machine that is already deleted is `404 not_found`.

409.description: The machine cannot be deleted yet; `details.kind` is `delete_blocked`.

200.description: Event page. A placement that failed has an event of kind `placement_failed`; its cause is on the host detail's `recentPlacementFailures`. A failed start that was retried as a new runner, other machines first, has an event of kind `placement_retried` on the machine where it failed.

get.description: The fleet's health over a window: the fleet and per-machine scores with their components, each machine's relative speed per runner size, CPU use by job category, the live queue and running counts, and the areas of concern (windowed and live, merged, worst first). Administrators only (a member gets `403 forbidden`). The response is cached per window for 30 seconds. A computation that fails, or takes over 2 seconds, counts as a failure: the last response is served with `stale: true` (a 200) while it is under 10 minutes old, and `503 dependency_unavailable` otherwise; after a failure the window is not computed again for 30 seconds, and serves the same stale response or 503 meanwhile. See docs/design/fleet-health.md.

put.summary: Save the pool's fleet execution profile
put.description: Saves the pool's fleet execution profile. An optional `hostIds` (a list of machine ids, at most 64) pins the pool to those machines; `[]` clears the pin, and leaving it out keeps the current pin. An optional `exclusiveLabels` (boolean) makes the pool's runners skip the catch-all `self-hosted-linux` / `self-hosted-macos` label; leaving it out keeps the current setting. See docs/fleet-api.md, Pinning a pool to machines and Exclusive pools.

put.description: The room GridOps may fill on the machine. Send any of `cpuMillis`, `memoryMib`, `diskBytes`; a figure left out is kept. Each must be greater than zero and no more than the machine reports, so a figure the machine has not reported cannot be set. A budget below what runners already hold is accepted: those runners finish, and nothing new is placed until enough room is free. Returns the budget now in force.

Revoke an API token (owner or system admin; idempotent)

post.description: Revokes the machine's credentials and stops it taking work; its history stays. Body: `{"expectedRevision": n}`. A browser session retires under the original rules (an administrator, the current revision, no placement still running). A token with `fleet:retire` (never implied by `fleet:operate`) may retire only a machine that cannot hurt a healthy fleet; otherwise it is refused with `409 host_not_retirable`, `details.kind = "retire_blocked"`, listing every reason in `details.reasons`: the lifecycle is `active` (`lifecycle_active`); it reported in within the quiet period, 15 minutes unless `GRIDOPS_TOKEN_RETIRE_MIN_OFFLINE_MINUTES` says otherwise (`recently_seen`); a placement is not cleaned up or failed, or capacity is still charged (`live_placement`); a start is unconfirmed (`unconfirmed_start`); a runner on it has not finished (`live_runner`); a command is waiting within its deadline (`pending_command`). The checks run in the retire transaction. Retiring a retired machine is a no-op. The audit row `fleet.host.retired` names the token.

409.description: A token may not retire this machine yet (`retire_blocked`), or the revision moved (`revision_conflict`).

get.summary: List the runner pools the caller may see
get.description: Paginated (`page`, `perPage`). A browser without a session gets `200` with `"authenticated": false` and no items; a token never does: it is accepted with `pools:read` or refused. Only pools on GitHub installations the token's owner can access are listed.

post.description: The body and its validation are exactly the web form's (`CreateRunnerPool`); a validation error is `400 { "error": "..." }` with the form's message, a duplicate name `409`. The owner must administer the pool's installation (or repositories), as in the browser; Bitbucket connections need a system administrator. A token request is not origin-checked. Audited as `runner_pool.created`, naming the token. Starts `desiredCount` runners as the form does. A pool that includes Tart clones the Tart base VM in `tartImage` (when Tart is the primary provider and `tartImage` is left out, `image` is used); the server default from `/api/v1/runner-pools/options` is never substituted. `image` and the primary provider's `dockerImage` or `tartImage`, when both are sent, must be the same value, or the request is refused with `400`. No image is stored for a provider the pool does not use: `dockerImage` or `tartImage` sent for one is ignored and reads back as `""`. Every provider in `providers` needs its image (Tart with `macosRuntime` `native` excepted, and Docker on a `gitlab`-scoped pool, which may leave `dockerImage` empty to run `gitlab/gitlab-runner:ubuntu-v19.6.0`), or the request is refused with `400` naming the field. `runnerGroupId` is used only by a GitHub `organization` pool, where it must be positive; other pools may leave it out.

get.summary: The pool form's options: installations the owner administers, Bitbucket connections (name and workspace only), defaults
Repositories the owner can put in a repository pool (asks GitHub)
Runner groups of an organization installation the owner administers (asks GitHub)
Repositories of an installation the owner administers (asks GitHub)
One runner pool, with its capacity and configuration
get.description: Includes the provisioning state: `state`, `provisionFailureCount`, `provisionRetryAt`, `provisionCircuitOpen`, and `provisionWaitReason`, the runner manager's reason while `state` is `waiting` (for a Tart VM, `Waiting for a macOS VM slot: position p of n in the queue. …` with who holds the Mac's slots) or why the pool's provider is unavailable while `state` is `provider-unavailable` (which provider, and whether its agent cannot be reached or answers with an error, for example `macOS (Tart) provider unavailable: its agent cannot be reached.`), otherwise `null`. A wait for a slot is not a failure and never counts towards the provisioning circuit. A pool whose latest start waits for capacity or a slot has `state` `waiting` (and its reason) even with earlier failures or `provisionCircuitOpen` `true`; only `paused`, `provisioning-paused`, `builtin-host-off` and `provider-unavailable` take precedence over it. `provider-unavailable`: the runner manager could not ask any provider the pool runs on (the Mac's Tart agent is asleep, down, or refuses the manager), so the reconciler skips the pool and leaves its runners as they are until the provider answers; the events of each pool that runs on that provider record `Runner provider unavailable` and, later, `Runner provider available again`, once each, and `Runner provider unavailable` once more if the way the provider fails changes (unreachable, or answering with an error). No reason or event names the agent's address. The circuit stays open while the pool waits, until a start succeeds or fails. The pool list carries the same fields.

put.description: The body and validation are the web form's (`UpdateRunnerPool`). The owner must administer every installation the pool uses. Audited as `runner_pool.updated`, naming the token. Images follow the create rules: `image` and the primary provider's `dockerImage` or `tartImage`, when both are sent, must be the same value (`400` otherwise); no image is kept for a provider the pool does not use; and adding a provider needs its image (`dockerImage`, or `tartImage` unless `macosRuntime` is `native`), never a server default, or the edit is refused with `400` naming the field (a GitLab pool may leave `dockerImage` empty, as on create). Dropping an image left over for an unused provider does not replace the pool's runners.

delete.summary: Remove a runner pool and its runners
delete.description: Refused with `409` while the pool still has runners on fleet machines. Removes the pool's runners on the built-in host, as the web app does. Audited as `runner_pool.deleted`, naming the token.

get.description: Read only. Built from the runner manager's health (`providers.tart.vmSlots`) and the runners and pools GridOps holds. Answers `200` whether or not a Tart agent is configured or reachable; `tartAgent` says which.

A pattern that does not compile, an empty pattern or one over 1 KiB is a 422 naming each such rule, and a list of over 200 rules is a 422 as a whole; nothing is saved. The save writes a `job_categories.updated` audit event with the lists before and after.
